body: Forward test of the promise-tracker credibility method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.58 (naive base rate 0.35) that: Walmart FY27 adjusted EPS is ≥$2.89 (top of its $2.84–2.89 guide). Evidence: Q3 FY27 earnings presentation (19-Nov-2026): FY27 adjusted EPS guide raised for the third time — $2.75–2.85 (Feb) → $2.80–2.87 (Aug) → $2.84–2.89 (Nov); net sales cc +4.9–5.2%; adjusted operating income cc +8.0–8.6%. Q3 adj EPS $0.65 (+4.8%); FY26 adjusted EPS base $2.64 (which, from memory, was above the top of its own final FY26 range of $2.58–2.63). Reasoning: Walmart has a recent habit of finishing at or above the top of its final guide, and has raised three times this year; holiday trends and tariff-refund noise are the risks. Resolution: YES if Walmart's reported FY27 adjusted EPS (Q4 FY27 earnings release) ≥ $2.89. Source: Walmart Q4 FY27 earnings 8-K (SEC EDGAR, CIK 104169). Resolve by 2027-03-01; score with Brier vs base rate.

body: Forward test of the sector cycle/lead indicator method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.55 (naive base rate 0.65) that: SBI Cards Q3 FY27 gross NPA ratio is ≤1.90% (no rise from Q2 FY27). Evidence: Q2 FY27 call (29-Oct-2026): GNPA 1.90% (−14 bps QoQ, −95 bps YoY), NNPA 0.77%, gross credit cost 5.6% (−98 bps QoQ); management overlay raised by ₹30 cr to ₹100 cr citing 'prolonged conflict in West Asia… higher energy prices, inflation and interest rates may impact household cash flows'; guide 'gross credit costs to stay around 6% for the current financial year' and 'we don't expect the credit costs to moderate much beyond' 5.5–6%; cost of funds 6.8% (+18 bps QoQ) and 'expected to increase over the next few quarters'; receivables ₹58,376 cr, festive spends to lift receivables in Q3. Screener GNPA: Jun-24 3.06%, Sep-24 3.27%, Dec-24 3.24%, Mar-25 3.08%, Jun-25 3.07%, Sep-25 2.85%, Dec-25 2.86%, Mar-26 2.41%, Jun-26 2.04%, Sep-26 1.90%. Reasoning: Lead indicator: RBI has hiked (repo 5.5%, more expected), fuel inflation is squeezing households, and management itself built an overlay and called the credit-cost bottom. Unsecured card delinquencies respond to rate/inflation shocks with a 1–3 quarter lag. Festive receivable growth (bigger denominator) helps the ratio, so we stay just above even, but below the trend-following base. Resolution: YES if SBI Cards and Payment Services' reported gross NPA ratio (% of gross advances/receivables) for the quarter ended 31-Dec-2026 is ≤1.90% (two decimals as reported). Source: SBI Cards Q3 FY27 results / investor presentation (NSE) / screener.in quarterly table. Resolve by 2027-02-15; score with Brier vs base rate.
